description: Evergreen tree or large shrub with dense, spiny branches and dark purple berries. Its presence is treated as an indicator of ecosystem health.
nativeStatus: Native to the Río de la Plata region
ecology: A core component of native woodland. The mariposa bandera argentina needs dense stands of it as a larval host, so scattered single plants are worth less than a group.
wildlifeNotes: Several bird species build nests in the spiny branches, where the thorns deter predators. The dark purple berries feed celestinos, zorzal chalchalero and frutero azul among others.
otherUses: The berries yield a dark dye. The wood is extremely hard and was traditionally used for fence posts that last decades.
sources: La biodiversidad urbana, Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires: https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/noticias/la-biodiversidad-urbana-el-corazon-verde-de-la-ciudad
